projects.name: Refugees and other crisis affected people in Uganda have access to adequate nutritious food in times of crisis
projects.description: This focuses on providing critical food and nutrition assistance to refugees and food-insecure local populations in the Karamoja sub-region and Southwestern Uganda. Uganda experienced climatic shocks, and a continuous refugee influx, which contributed to increased needs. WFP partnered with stakeholders including the Government, UNHCR and cooperating partners, to improve food access, ensure that refugees receive adequate and nutritious food, and promote their financial inclusion. Additionally, food-insecure households in Karamoja benefited from early action interventions, providing both food assistance and nutrition support. WFP also extended food and cash assistance to communities affected by mudslides and floods in Kasese and Ntoroko districts.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services

projects.name: Food insecure populations in areas affected by recurring climate shocks have access to adequate and nutritious food all year
projects.description: WFP aims to ensure food-insecure populations in climate-affected areas have year-round access to adequate and nutritious food. Through its livelihood and resilience-building programme, WFP provided technical assistance to the Government and supported men and women to establish community assets while strengthening the national social protection system for livelihood and resilience programs. Under the school feeding programme, WFP provided nutritious school meals to improve education access, retention, and learning outcomes, while offering technical support to the Government to foster national ownership. These efforts align with Uganda’s Third National Development Plan (NDP III) and aim to establish a sustainable, government-led Home-Grown School Feeding (HGSF) model which focuses on procuring food locally from SHFs to enhance community resilience and support local food systems. projects.name: Provide technical and financial support for Restoration and Management of Wetland Hydrology and Associated Catchments.
projects.description:
At country level, the Programme is designed to contribute to sustainable natural resource management, ecosystem and community resilience to climate change and livelihood improvement. The main objective is to protect, restore and maintain the integrity of degraded fragile ecosystems and increasing the country's resilience to impacts of climate change. The programme implementation started in 2018 and is expected to end in 2026. Specifically, the outcomes anticipated out of these efforts include:
1) Restoration and management of wetland hydrology and associated catchments
2) Improved agricultural practices and alternative livelihood options in the wetland and catchment
3) Strengthening access to climate and early warning information to farmers and other communities to support wetland management.

This is responsible for strengthening institutions and systems to deliver social protection programmes and is delivered through the Child Sensitive Social Protection Programme (CSSP).
